CarrierPony protects every message and file with OpenPGP, a battle-tested encryption standard. Here\'s what that means for you, in plain language.

When you set up CarrierPony, your device creates a key pair: a public key you share by pairing, and a private key that never leaves your device. Anyone can lock a message with your public key, but only your private key can unlock it.

Messages and files are encrypted on your device before they are sent, and only decrypted on your contact\'s device. The relay in between forwards sealed envelopes and cannot read them — neither can we.
Encryption only helps if you\'re talking to the right person. Compare the safety number with your contact over a call or in person; if it matches on both devices, no one is sitting between you.

Keep the app lock on. Back up your identity and store the passphrase somewhere safe. Verify your contacts, and share invites only over channels you trust. If you lose your device, restore from your backup and pair again.
CarrierPony\'s cryptography is built on PGPonyCore, which is open source — anyone can inspect exactly how the encryption works.
Relay reachable and speaking the protocol

Must be an https address. You can only exchange messages with people whose app points at the same relay, so switch before you pair, or re-pair afterward. A self-hosted relay can\'t send push notifications, so you\'ll receive messages when CarrierPony is open.
Quit and reopen CarrierPony to connect to the new relay. Your identity stays on this device, but you\'ll need to pair again with contacts on the new relay.
Quit and reopen CarrierPony for the change to take effect.
Must be an https address. Your identity will register on this relay, and you\'ll only be able to reach people on the same one. A self-hosted relay can\'t send push notifications.
Your identity will register on this relay when you create it. You can change it later in Settings.

A relay you run yourself can\'t send push notifications. Turn this on to be woken through CarrierPony\'s push service instead. It only ever receives a signal that a message is waiting, never the sender or the message. Left off, you get messages when the app is open.

This erases this account\'s messages, contacts, and keys from this device. It can\'t be undone.

Separate accounts keep their messages and contacts apart on this device. They don\'t hide from the relay that both come from the same device and network, so anyone watching the relay could still tell they\'re linked.
Reach contacts on this Wi-Fi without the relay. This shares your device\'s local IP with a contact you message directly. Off keeps everything on the relay.
A message delivered directly won\'t also go through the relay. The person\'s other devices and offline delivery won\'t receive it.
Early test (2.2): connect to contacts directly over the internet, with the relay only introducing you. This shares your IP with a contact you message directly. Off keeps everything on the relay.

Also post each message to the peer\'s sealed mailbox on public Nostr relays, so delivery does not depend only on your relay. Those third-party relays see opaque content under a rotating tag, and they see this device\'s IP. Off by default.
Regenerate this account\'s sealed keys and re-sync with your contacts. Use it if messages stop arriving after you or a contact reinstalled.
This regenerates your sealed keys and re-syncs with every contact. Your messages and identity are not affected. If a single pair is stuck, run this on both devices.
Your sealed keys were regenerated and shared with your contacts. Give it about a minute, then try sending again.
No relays set. Nostr delivery stays off until you add at least one.

These are the public Nostr relays this app posts to and reads from for the extra delivery path. Each one sees opaque content under a rotating tag, plus this device\'s IP. Add relays you trust, or point them at your own.

Deliver to a contact over SMS when you have their number, for when there is no internet. Messages are chunked across silent data SMS. Your carrier sees that data messages went to that number, and standard SMS rates apply. Off by default.
Messages to this contact can also go over SMS to this number when the other paths are down. It is stored only on this device. Include the country code.
